report_interpretation: Premiums, longevity, stipends, differentials, and specialty pay are distinct channels that base-wage comparisons can miss.
Direct values and schedules are abundant, but pay basis, period, unit, rank, and base/non-base alignment remain essential.
Effective dates, delayed implementation, and retroactive payments can change when negotiated gains are realized.
Scheduled percentage increases, COLA/CPI clauses, and step progression provide documentable growth rules.
Bargaining, arbitration, factfinding, settlements, and strike constraints are plausible institutional channels, not causal estimates.
Structured ladders and classifications shape progression and complicate cross-occupation comparisons.
Work-stoppage constraints form part of institutional bargaining context.
Comparability, recruitment, retention, and staffing language appear as stated compensation justifications.
Some spans point toward a safety-side advantage, but directional evidence is sparse and uneven.
Budget, appropriation, and approval language documents constraints without identifying effects.
